title: A creation walk
hook: a weekly walk to notice God's world
tomorrow: why did Paul want the money set aside before he arrived?

segments.voice: Yesterday, a letter: one name, one thing seen. Your line was encourage. Today the week's practices step outside.

Earbuds in, podcast on, eyes on the sidewalk, and by the time you're home you haven't seen a single thing. Now a hillside, and a crowd full of the same worries people carry on any sidewalk: what will we eat, what will we wear. Jesus doesn't hand them a plan. He points up, at birds crossing the sky: “Behold the fowls of the air.” Then he looks down at the wildflowers in the grass, and says something startling about a king.
screen: `EARBUDS IN, EYES DOWN.` → `WHAT WILL WE EAT? WEAR?` → `BEHOLD THE FOWLS OF THE AIR.` → `THEN, THE FLOWERS.`

segments.voice: First the birds, in the King James Bible: “Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them.” Then the flowers, and the king: “Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin: And yet I say unto you, That even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.” Solomon in all his glory loses to a wildflower. Here's what to notice: Jesus answers worry with an assignment for the eyes. Behold. Consider. How they grow. Not a glance on the way past; looking long enough to see something. The setting matters too. Just before, he says: “Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink.” The lilies aren't decoration. They're his argument. The Psalms read the world the same way, as something that speaks: “The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork.” A creation walk takes that seriously, once a week. No headphones, no step count to beat. Just a slow walk where the sky, a tree, or a weed in a crack gets a full look, and for those who pray, the looking turns into thanks.
screen: `THEY SOW NOT, YET ARE FED.` · `SOLOMON LOSES TO A WILDFLOWER.` · `AN ASSIGNMENT FOR THE EYES.` · `THE HEAVENS DECLARE.` · then, large: `CONSIDER THE LILIES.`

segments.voice: Stand and walk for a minute, to a window, a door, or out onto a step, with nothing in your ears. Find one living thing, a tree, a weed, a bird, the sky, and give it a full look: how it grows, what color it really is. If you pray, let the looking turn into thanks.
A creation walk. A weekly slow walk with the headphones out, where looking at what grows becomes a way to set worry down.
The line to take with you: consider the lilies, how they grow, dressed finer than Solomon ever was. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1702 COUNTS.` → `LIVING IT · 21 OF 70.` → `TOMORROW: WHY DID PAUL WANT THE MONEY SET ASIDE BEFORE HE CAME?`

howItsDone: Some Christians take a regular slow walk outdoors, without music or podcasts, to notice creation and give thanks, sometimes carrying a line from Matthew 6 or a psalm with them.

chat.says: walked Pop's loop with him, no earbuds. he stopped at every weed. why does he LOOK at stuff so long?
options: Consider the lilies, how they grow: look long enough to see. Pop's doing that.
He's slow from the surgery. It's just recovery, nothing spiritual about it.
Nature's nice, but staring at weeds is a distraction from real prayer.
chat.meaning: Jesus' words are behold and consider: a long look at what grows. Psalm 19 says the heavens declare the glory of God.

fowls.meaning: in the King James wording: birds

Solomon.meaning: a king of Israel, remembered for his wisdom and splendor

firmament.meaning: the sky, pictured as a great dome

notes: Written 2026-10-13 in the year-2-4 recipe; rewritten 2026-10-15 in recipe v3 (shape: story; the hillside scene stops as Jesus turns to the flowers, and the teach finishes it; practice: a one-minute walk).

The hillside scene (a crowd, birds overhead, wildflowers in the grass) is framing; Matthew 5:1 sets the sermon on a mountain, and the birds and flowers are in Jesus' words, not described as present. Confirm the framing is acceptable.
Which flower Jesus meant by 'lilies' is uncertain; the lesson says 'wildflowers' and names none.
